prompt:
Scene:
A square architectural photograph at late afternoon with a 35mm tilt-shift lens, eye level at the far end of a wet cobblestone plaza. Golden warm light rakes the front facade from camera-right; the sky is a clean gradient from pale peach at the horizon to deep teal overhead.

Subject:
A full-scale gothic cathedral, 90 meters tall, entirely carved from a single uninterrupted slab of translucent bottle-green glass. Flying buttresses, rose window, pointed arches, and twin bell towers all read as continuous glass mass with no seams, no stained-glass inserts, no metal frames. Because the walls are translucent, the warm interior lighting (visible as diffused amber glow) is clearly seen through the entire building, turning the cathedral into a green lantern.

Important details:
Realistic thick-glass behavior: edges read darker green due to increased optical path; thinner detailed flourishes (pinnacles, tracery) read almost clear. Subsurface scattering softens all shadow boundaries. The wet plaza is a faithful reflection showing the inverted cathedral in near-perfect mirror. Scale anchor: three pedestrians with long coats crossing at lower left, 1.8 meters tall, human figures reading as tiny silhouettes against the glass wall.

Use case:
Reference image for the Glass Cathedral cycle. Later images must preserve this exact cathedral silhouette, camera angle, plaza, and pedestrian positions while changing interior lighting and weather.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio, no real-world cathedral names, no crosses with visible branded iconography, no stylized painterly rendering, no polygonal CGI facets visible on the glass.

description: The hero translucent green-glass gothic cathedral at late afternoon glowing from within.
